{{Short description|Soviet mathematician (1903–1979)}}
{{other people||Andrei Markov (disambiguation){{!}}Andrei Markov}}

'''Andrey Andreyevich Markov''' ({{langx|ru|Андре́й Андре́евич Ма́рков}}; 22 September 1903, [[Saint Petersburg]] &ndash; 11 October 1979, [[Moscow]]) was a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] [[mathematician]], the son of the Russian mathematician [[Andrey Markov|Andrey Markov Sr]], and one of the key founders of the Russian school of [[Constructivism (philosophy of mathematics)|constructive mathematics]] and logic. He made outstanding contributions to various areas of mathematics, including [[differential equation]]s, [[topology]], [[mathematical logic]] and the [[foundations of mathematics]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Kushner|first=Boris A|title=The constructive mathematics of A. A. Markov|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|volume=113|year=2006|issue=6|pages=559&ndash;566|mr=2231143|jstor=27641983|doi=10.2307/27641983}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|mr=2069985|last1=Glukhov|first1=M. M.|last2=Nagornyĭ|first2=N. M.|title=Andreĭ Andreevich Markov (on the centenary of his birth)|journal=Diskrete Math. Appl.|volume=14|year=2004|issue=1|pages=1&ndash;6|doi=10.1515/156939204774148776|s2cid=120486293}}</ref>

His name is in particular associated with [[Markov's principle]] and [[Markov's principle#Markov's rule|Markov's rule]] in mathematical logic, [[Markov theorem|Markov's theorem]] in [[knot theory]] and [[Markov algorithm]] in [[theoretical computer science]].

An important result that he proved in 1947 was that the [[Semi-Thue system#The word problem for semi-Thue systems|word problem for semigroups]] was unsolvable; [[Emil Leon Post]] obtained the same result independently at about the same time.

In 1953 he became a member of the [[Communist Party of the Soviet Union|Communist Party]].

In 1960, Markov obtained fundamental results showing that the classification of four-dimensional [[manifold]]s is [[Undecidable problem|undecidable]]: no general algorithm exists for distinguishing two arbitrary manifolds with four or more dimensions. This is because four-dimensional manifolds have sufficient flexibility to allow us to embed any algorithm within their structure. Hence, classifying all four-manifolds would imply a solution to Turing's [[halting problem]]. Embedding implies failure to create a correspondence between algorithms and indexing (naturally uncountably infinite, but even larger) of the four-manifolds structure. Failure is in Cantor's sense. Indexing is in Godel's sense.

His doctoral students include [[Boris Kushner (mathematician)|Boris Kushner]], [[Gennady Makanin]], and [[Nikolai Shanin]].

== Awards and honors ==

* [[Medal "For Valiant Labour in the Great Patriotic War 1941–1945"]] (1945)
* [[Order of the Badge of Honour]] (1945)
* [[Medal "For the Defence of Leningrad"]] (1946)
* [[Order of Lenin]] (1954)
* [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]] (1963)
